newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEAKER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed easier against hard currencies on Thursday on the back of slight import pressure, dealers said.

"We saw a quite a bit of buying from the early part of the morning to mid afternoon and that pushed prices up by about two cents," one dealer said, adding however: "But later on, almost at the close of trade, some banks started selling."

Dealers said trade during the day was hampered by a communications fault on the Post and Telecommunications Corporation linked dealing machines, which also contributed to the local unit's depreciation against the key U.S. dollar.
"Trade was really difficult because our machines were down most of the day and we had to use the phones. Some people started quoting high just to protect their positions," said one dealer.
At Thursday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar, which peaked at 10.9700/9800 during the day, was quoted at 10.9650/9750 versus the U.S. dollar, down from 10.9500/9600 on Wednesday.
It also fell to 17.9800/18.0100 from 17.8000/8200 against sterling, partly tracking a weaker U.S. dollar on that unit overseas and was at 6.6400/6500 against the mark, down from 6.6300/6500.
Against South Africa's rand it also slipped to 2.4515/4555 from 2.4400/4600. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsro m: +263-4 72 52 28/9
